title: The sync gate refuses every commit that writes under an internal root or pointer in any clone with an upstream, although only publish to the public home must refuse a team's own internal root
goal: kg_sync's range tree-cause check refuses internal-root and pointer writes only where the clone publishes to a public home, and keeps the _private and _cache causes everywhere, or git.md states that sync refuses them
repro_reason: a design question for the operator first: the planted input is in the notes
notes: SP-mut2pmu3 review gap 7 (S3, a design question for the operator). kg_sync.py:850-862 now prints refused for every commit of UP..HEAD that writes under an internal root, an internal pointer or its gitlink (kbpublic.range_tree_causes, added by BG-thhbfbx4). A team's own internal root lands on the integration remote by kbgit.py sync --push, so in a group clone that holds internal roots the gate blocks that sync for good; only publish to the public home must refuse it. Planted: base commit, then a commit adding kb/team/_root.md (visibility: internal) and kb/team/b.md: range_tree_causes(base, repo) returns causes and the gate FAILS. This repo has no internal root, so its own sync is unaffected. Fix options: run it only where the clone publishes (kbpublic.publish_remote set), or keep only the _private and _cache causes for the integration remote, or say in git.md that sync refuses internal-root commits.
